Two rectangles is more "pause". Square and hexagon are more "stop"-ish. If that makes any sense.

Square and two rectangles come from audiocassettes where "stop" (square) retracted the read head and halted the tape while "pause" (two rectangles) halted the tape but left the read head extended. With modern media players the convention has become that stop will lose the current position in a track while pause will allow you to resume playing exactly where you left off.

The octagon is from traffic and is octagonal so its shape is uniquely identifiable even if covered (with snow for example) or if viewed from the rear.

The square (stop) and two pales (pause) actually predate audiocasettes.

The square represents a frame of video. The two pales represent the spot between two frames of video (where you might literally cut and paste).

Edit: also, the octagon shape of the stop-sign represents the level of caution required at the traffic stop (just like Hazardous Materials Information System in the workplace); a yield sign is a triangle and a go sign is a circle. The more sides the sign, the more hazardous the intersection.
